plan.summary: Fix Windows compatibility issue where os.fchmod() raises AttributeError on Windows
plan.root_cause: os.fchmod() is a Unix-only function that doesn't exist on Windows. Calling it unconditionally causes save() to fail on Windows with AttributeError.
plan.solution: Add platform check using hasattr(os, 'fchmod') before calling os.fchmod(). On Windows, tempfile.mkstemp already creates files with restricted permissions, so the security intent is maintained.
plan.test_strategy: Create regression tests that simulate Windows by removing os.fchmod and verify save() works correctly
implementation_sequence: 1. Create failing test that simulates Windows (no fchmod)
2. Add hasattr check before calling os.fchmod in storage.py
verification_commands: uv run ruff check src/flywheel/storage.py tests/test_issue_6938_windows_compat.py

implementation.risks: None - minimal change with clear platform-specific guard
